scenario: Turn a stack of receipt photos into a clean March expense report.
did: Read each receipt for date, merchant, amount, and category, and total them.
why: The rubric checks are sound and the amounts verify (the corrected Butcher $31.45, Progressive $215.00, the $312.15 total). The issue is the input images: the 'receipts I snapped on my phone' are actually clean template renders — identical fonts, flat backgrounds, no photo or paper artifacts — so the task doesn't really test reading real-world receipts. C7 also just penalizes the opposite of what C1-C3 reward.
fix: Replace the template-style receipts with realistic phone photos of actual receipts (normal lighting, angles, paper), and merge C7 into C1-C3.

scenario: Write a warehouse inventory report from pallet and package photos.
did: Count packages per pallet type, total the month-end inventory, and check PR/YKF delivery times.
why: The per-pallet counts (A=20, B=72, C=96), the month-end total (1,504), and the PR estimated-vs-actual deltas all check out. One thing: C7 locks in a single reading of the ambiguous 'treat all times as UTC' instruction (converting the YKF arrival to 19:30) on a high-value check, when reading it as 13:30 is also defensible.
fix: Loosen C7 to accept either reading of the YKF arrival time, or make the timezone instruction unambiguous.
